intro: Week 7 opens Thursday night with the Patriots at the Bears, and the news cycle is heavy on the AFC South and the Eagles. Indianapolis fired general manager Chris Ballard, Philadelphia lost Jalen Hurts for what looks like the season, and San Francisco, Kansas City and Minnesota sit unbeaten. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Colts fire GM Chris Ballard after loss to winless Titans
top.dek: Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon made the move Monday, a day after Indianapolis blew a 13-0 halftime lead and fell to 2-4. Assistant GM Ed Dodds will run the personnel department during the search. Coach Shane Steichen now reports to ownership, which puts his job in question.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Eagles place Jalen Hurts on IR with blood clots in his lungs
top.dek: Doctors found clots in his lungs along with a deep vein thrombosis, and the earliest he can return is Week 11 against the Steelers. The team and his agent expect a full recovery. Tanner McKee takes over for an Eagles team that has lost four straight.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Kyler Gordon debuts with three sacks and a game-sealing strip
top.dek: Gordon returned from a calf injury and sacked Michael Penix Jr. three times, two of them strip-sacks. The second forced a fumble that Devin Bush recovered at the Atlanta 28 with 2:54 left. Chicago won 31-23 to reach 4-2.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 34: straight field goals made by Vikings kicker Will Reichard
top.dek: Reichard hit three more against the Saints before Minnesota's bye and carries the streak into Sunday's game against the Colts. Andrew Van Ginkel's sack also extended the Vikings' run of games with at least one sack to 33.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Patriots visit the Bears on Thursday Night Football
top.dek: New England plays at Soldier Field on Thursday, Oct. 22, at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video, with both teams at 4-2. The Patriots have won three straight but arrive on a short week with a thin offensive line. Drake Maye and Caleb Williams meet for the second time.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills survive Vegas shootout, head to bye

stories.text: Bills outlast Raiders 33-30 to reach 5-1
stories.summary: Buffalo and Las Vegas were tied 13-13 at halftime, and the Bills made the late plays in a 33-30 win at Allegiant Stadium. Josh Allen threw for 255 yards and two touchdowns, including a 12-yard shovel pass to Keon Coleman. The defense forced incompletions on the final Raiders drive and got a punt.

stories.text: Moore and Oliver expected back after the bye
stories.summary: Receiver DJ Moore and defensive tackle Ed Oliver should return in Week 8, according to the coaches' Monday updates. Cornerback Dee Alford played about 40 snaps at nickel despite an ankle injury. Right tackle Spencer Brown, who hurt his back against the Rams, was a full participant before the Raiders game and was expected to play.

stories.text: James Cook runs for 95 and the go-ahead score
stories.summary: Cook carried 22 times for 95 yards and scored the three-yard go-ahead touchdown in the fourth quarter. He also caught three passes for 58 yards. Linebacker Dorian Williams added the first interception of his career, jumping a Kirk Cousins throw early in the third quarter.

stories.text: 258: Josh Allen ties Jim Kelly for Bills TD record
stories.summary: Allen's 12-yard touchdown pass to Coleman was the 258th of his career, which ties Jim Kelly for the most passing touchdowns in Buffalo history. One more puts him alone at the top, and the Bills do not play again until Nov. 1.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then Ravens at home Nov. 1
stories.summary: Buffalo is off in Week 7 and returns in Week 8 at home against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1 p.m. ET. Safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson is suspended one game for spitting at an opponent, so he is set to miss that Ravens game unless an appeal succeeds. Davison Igbinosun, who had three pass breakups against Las Vegas, has earned most of the snaps at boundary corner.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Winless Dolphins return from the bye at the Jets

stories.text: Hafley sticks with Willis at 0-5
stories.summary: Miami is winless and coming off a bye after a 31-24 loss to Cincinnati. Coach Jeff Hafley said Malik Willis remains the starter and that Kyle McCord is not under consideration. Hafley also called ball security a bye-week focus, with Willis carrying five fumbles through five games.

stories.text: Achane stays on IR as bye-week list grows
stories.summary: Running back De'Von Achane remains on injured reserve with a knee injury and is not expected to play against the Jets, so Ollie Gordon II stays the lead back. Right guard Jonah Savaiinaea (ankle), linebacker Jordyn Brooks, edge Robert Beal Jr., cornerback Reese Taylor, back Jaylen Wright and receiver Caleb Douglas sat out Tuesday's voluntary practice, and some of that may be precaution. Miami has not issued an official Week 7 report.

stories.text: Rookie CB Chris Johnson keeps climbing
stories.summary: Johnson earned an 86.9 PFF grade against the Bengals, his third straight game at 69 or better after two games under 50. He forced a fumble in the second half with a punch at the ball. He also won an appeal of a $17,911 fine for a hip-drop tackle, and the league removed one of his three strikes in that category.

stories.text: 0: leads held by Miami this season
stories.summary: The Dolphins have not led in any of their five games. That sits one short of the NFL record of six games without a lead, set by the 2005 Texans. Opponents are also completing 76.0% of their passes against Miami, which is on pace to break the 72.7% record the 2016 Lions set.

stories.text: At the Jets, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Miami visits the New York Jets (2-4) at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Watch whether the Jets pass rush, with David Bailey at five sacks, gets home against a Miami line that has allowed sacks on 9.72% of pass attempts. Willis has thrown four interceptions through five games.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Patriots win three straight, now face a short week

stories.text: Patriots beat Jets 26-19 for a third straight win
stories.summary: New England moved to 4-2 with a 26-19 win over the Jets at Gillette Stadium. The Patriots led 17-3 at halftime and held on after the Jets cut it to 17-13 in the third quarter. Corey Kiner carried eight straight times on a 13-play field goal drive that ate 6:08 in the fourth quarter.

stories.text: Doubs to IR, line thinned for Thursday
stories.summary: Receiver Romeo Doubs hurt his shoulder after a 42-yard touchdown catch and went on injured reserve. Tackle Morgan Moses (ankle), guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and lineman Ben Brown (knee) left the game early. On Monday's practice report, Brown and Vera-Tucker did not participate, Moses was limited, and the team has not issued game designations.

stories.text: Drake Maye throws three touchdowns
stories.summary: Maye went 18 of 32 for 235 yards and three touchdowns against the Jets, two of them to Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas. A.J. Brown returned after a four-game absence and caught 3 of 10 targets for 27 yards. Cornerback Christian Gonzalez also returned and allowed two catches for 20 yards against Garrett Wilson.

stories.text: 5.5: sacks for Elijah Ponder through six games
stories.summary: Ponder picked up a sack against the Jets and now has 5.5 through six games. New England finished with three sacks on the day. Tackle Caleb Lomu played 59 snaps and gave up zero pressures against David Bailey's 16 rushes.

stories.text: At Bears, Thursday 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video
stories.summary: New England plays at Soldier Field in Chicago on Thursday, Oct. 22, at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video, with both teams at 4-2. The short week leaves the offensive line short on bodies, and Coach Mike Vrabel said the team must find 48 to put on the field. Caleb Lomu could make his first NFL start if Moses cannot go.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets fall short at New England, host Miami next

stories.text: Jets fall 26-19 at New England after a slow half
stories.summary: The Jets dropped to 2-4 after trailing 17-3 at halftime in Foxborough. New England scored 10 points in the final two minutes of the first half. New York cut the gap to 17-13 in the third quarter but turned the ball over on downs twice, on fourth-and-2 and fourth-and-1.

stories.text: Hall, Mitchell, Parham and Ossai out vs. Patriots
stories.summary: Running back Breece Hall (quad), receiver Adonai Mitchell, left guard Dylan Parham and edge Joseph Ossai were ruled out against New England. Coach Aaron Glenn called both Hall and Mitchell week-to-week earlier in the week. Receiver Omar Cooper Jr. returned from an ankle injury and played.

stories.text: Rookie Omar Cooper Jr. breaks out in his return
stories.summary: Cooper caught six passes for more than 100 yards and a 48-yard touchdown from Geno Smith, his first NFL score and first 100-yard game. He came back from an ankle injury that sent him to injured reserve after the opener. Braelon Allen added 78 yards on 17 carries with Hall out.

stories.text: 166: Geno Smith attempts before first interception
stories.summary: Smith's interception against the Patriots was his first of the season, ending a run of 166 pass attempts without one. He finished 20 of 30 for 252 yards and a touchdown. Kicker Jason Sanders hit four field goals, from 42, 40, 36 and 36 yards.

stories.text: Dolphins visit MetLife Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Jets host winless Miami on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at MetLife Stadium. New York will want Hall's status clarified and a better start after the Patriots opened a 14-point halftime lead. Miami has allowed a 76.55% completion rate, which sets up Smith and Garrett Wilson.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens blow a 10-0 lead to Cleveland

stories.text: Ravens fall 13-10 to Browns after scoring on first two drives
stories.summary: Baltimore led 10-0 after the first quarter and never scored again. Tyler Huntley, starting for the second straight week, finished 19 of 31 for 165 yards, and Andre Szmyt kicked a 37-yard field goal as time expired. Cleveland now sits alone atop the AFC North, and all of Baltimore's remaining games are against division rivals.

stories.text: Lamar Jackson still day-to-day with ankle sprain
stories.summary: Jackson has not practiced since hurting his ankle on Oct. 4 and sat out Sunday's loss. Coach Jesse Minter called him day-to-day, and Yahoo lists him as questionable for Cincinnati. Wednesday's practice will give the first real read on whether he plays.

stories.text: Derrick Henry takes the blame after fumble and 58 yards
stories.summary: Henry carried 17 times for 58 yards, his lowest total of the season, and fumbled in the fourth quarter after Carson Schwesinger forced the ball loose. Cleveland turned it into the tying touchdown. Henry owned the mistake in the locker room.

stories.text: 5: Straight Ravens games decided by a touchdown or less
stories.summary: Every one of Baltimore's last five games has ended within seven points. The Ravens also have not scored a second-half touchdown in either of their two losses this season. They have lost leads they could not close out.

stories.text: Ravens host Bengals Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Baltimore plays Cincinnati at home on Sunday, Oct. 25, with CBS carrying the game. Watch Jackson's practice status first, then whether the Ravens can run the ball after Henry's 58-yard day. Buffalo and Jacksonville follow the Bengals.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals return from bye with Ravens next

stories.text: Bengals come off bye needing a win at Baltimore
stories.summary: Cincinnati sits at 3-2 and, per Local 12, last in a tight AFC North after losing at Pittsburgh. Zac Taylor said the bye gave the team a chance to cut turnovers and create a scoring chance on every drive. A loss in Baltimore would put the Bengals 0-2 in the division.

stories.text: Tanner Hudson out for year with torn pectoral muscle
stories.summary: Hudson hurt his pectoral against Miami on Oct. 11 and his agent says he will miss the rest of the season. Linebacker Swayze Bozeman went to injured reserve with a broken forearm, and Kyle Dugger is week to week with a quad injury. Nearly the whole roster practiced Monday.

stories.text: Joe Burrow throws four touchdowns in win at Miami
stories.summary: Burrow went 23 of 32 for 190 yards and four scores, to Mike Gesicki, Samaje Perine, Hudson and Ja'Marr Chase. Three came in the first half. Chase's one-armed 45-yard catch in the end zone was his 58th career touchdown.

stories.text: 22: Evan McPherson's franchise-record field goal streak
stories.summary: McPherson made his 22nd consecutive field goal in the 31-24 win over Miami, a Bengals record. The streak carries into Baltimore after the bye. Jordan Battle also picked off Miami twice on back-to-back drives.

stories.text: Bengals at Ravens Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cincinnati visits Baltimore on Oct. 25 for its first meeting with the Ravens this season. Jim Nantz and JJ Watt call it on CBS. Watch how Burrow handles a Baltimore team that may start Tyler Huntley again.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns take AFC North lead on late kick

stories.text: Browns beat Ravens 13-10 and move into first in AFC North
stories.summary: Deshaun Watson led the winning drive, and Andre Szmyt hit a 37-yard field goal as time expired. Cleveland is 4-2 and 2-0 in the division. The offense stalled for most of the first half, and the defense carried the team.

stories.text: Judkins and Graham miss Ravens game; Schwesinger plays
stories.summary: Running back Quinshon Judkins tested his ankle before kickoff and sat out. Defensive tackle Mason Graham missed a second straight game with knee and ankle injuries, and Mike Hall Jr. stayed out. Linebacker Carson Schwesinger played through an ankle problem. Week 7 reports are not out yet.

stories.text: Carson Schwesinger forces game-changing Henry fumble
stories.summary: Schwesinger forced Derrick Henry's fourth-quarter fumble, which set up the tying touchdown. He finished with 13 tackles and nine defensive stops. Cleveland's defense also nearly intercepted Baltimore twice.

stories.text: 130: Browns net yards in the fourth quarter vs. Baltimore
stories.summary: Cleveland had three points and 107 net yards through three quarters. It gained 130 in the fourth and converted several third downs to win. Watson was sacked five times in the game.

stories.text: Browns at Titans Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Cleveland visits 1-5 Tennessee at Nissan Stadium on Oct. 25. The Titans rank last in points and yards per game through Week 5, and Cleveland's pass rush has 16 sacks. The Browns have also allowed sacks at the league's highest rate, so watch Jeffery Simmons.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers rally from 13 down, win in OT

stories.text: Steelers rally from 13 down to beat Bucs 26-19 in overtime
stories.summary: Pittsburgh trailed 16-3 entering the fourth quarter, scored on five straight possessions and won on Aaron Rodgers' six-yard touchdown pass to Germie Bernard. It was the Steelers' first comeback from a 13-point deficit since 1992. They are 4-2 heading to Paris.

stories.text: McCarthy twists ankle; Steelers carry long injury list
stories.summary: Coach Mike McCarthy hurt his ankle in the first half, spent halftime in the medical tent and returned for the second half. Wide receivers Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek were out with hand and calf injuries, and Pat Freiermuth, Keeanu Benton and Rico Dowdle went into the game questionable. Pittsburgh has not released Week 7 designations.

stories.text: Jalen Ramsey tallies 10 tackles and two sacks in OT win
stories.summary: Ramsey, who has played through a broken wrist, finished with 10 tackles and two sacks. His fourth-and-eight sack in overtime ended Tampa Bay's last real chance. Bernard caught 11 passes for 87 yards in the same game.

stories.text: 11: Germie Bernard catches on 12 targets vs. Tampa Bay
stories.summary: The rookie caught 11 of 12 targets for 87 yards and the overtime winner. Rodgers went 33 of 49 for 253 yards and two touchdowns, with five sacks taken. Bernard's role grew with Wilson and Skowronek out.

stories.text: Steelers face Saints in Paris Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET
stories.summary: Pittsburgh plays New Orleans at Stade de France on Oct. 25, with NFL Network carrying the game. The Saints are the designated home team and sit at 2-4 after beating the Giants. Watch how the Steelers handle a long trip after an overtime game.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Fairbairn's kick wins it in London

stories.text: Texans win a shootout in London on a last-second field goal
stories.summary: Ka'imi Fairbairn hit a 49-yard field goal as time expired, and Houston beat Jacksonville 34-31 at Wembley. C.J. Stroud went 24 of 34 for 312 yards and three touchdowns against a Jaguars defense that had allowed 20 points or fewer in every game this season. The win moves Houston to 2-4.

stories.text: Dell set to return as Houston sorts out its absences
stories.summary: Tank Dell is expected to be activated from injured reserve and play against the Giants, his first game in more than two years. Safety Reed Blankenship is in the concussion protocol. Jalen Pitre and running back David Montgomery were out in London, and the injury report for Week 7 is not out yet.

stories.text: Jaylin Noel posts four catches and 107 yards
stories.summary: Noel turned in the biggest receiving day on a Houston offense that scored touchdowns on three of four drives from the second quarter on. He caught four passes for 107 yards and a touchdown in London. Coach DeMeco Ryans singled out a Stroud throw to Noel at the end of the first half, made under pressure from Dennis Gardeck.

stories.text: 35.6%: Houston's snaps with six or more linemen
stories.summary: The Texans used six or more offensive linemen on 35.6 percent of their plays against Jacksonville. That is the highest rate by any team in a game this season. The heavy looks helped Houston score 34 points, the most the Jaguars have allowed since Week 10 of 2025.

stories.text: Giants visit Houston Sunday, Oct. 25, 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Houston hosts the Giants (3-2-1) in Week 7 on Fox. Ryans said the defense has to tackle better against New York's physical running backs. Watch whether Dell and Marvin Harrison Jr. both get real snaps in a receiver group that is finally getting healthy.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts fire GM Chris Ballard after 2-4 start

stories.text: Colts fire GM Chris Ballard after a loss to winless Tennessee
stories.summary: Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon fired Ballard on Monday, a day after Indianapolis blew a 13-0 halftime lead to the Titans. Assistant GM Ed Dodds will oversee the personnel department while the team searches for a replacement. Coach Shane Steichen and his staff will report to ownership, which leaves his own job status as the next question.

stories.text: Sauce Gardner diagnosed with mild calf strain
stories.summary: An MRI on Monday showed a mild left calf strain for Gardner, who left the Titans game in the third quarter and did not return. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported he is week to week. The Colts expect no long absence, but he looks likely to miss Sunday's game at Minnesota.

stories.text: Akeem Davis-Gaither leads a defense that deserved better
stories.summary: Davis-Gaither made nine tackles and three stops, and PFF graded him at 90.4 on 45 snaps, the best mark on the defense. Tennessee targeted him once in coverage and did not complete the pass. The unit held the Titans to 64 yards at halftime before the offense and special teams let the game slip.

stories.text: 6: sacks Tennessee piled on Daniel Jones
stories.summary: Jones went 22 of 42 for 269 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions while taking six sacks. Jeffery Simmons alone had seven pressures and two sacks. Jones now has four touchdowns and six interceptions on the season, per NFL.com.

stories.text: Colts visit unbeaten Vikings Sunday, Oct. 25, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Indianapolis travels to U.S. Bank Stadium to face Minnesota, which is 5-0. The Colts then face Jacksonville on Nov. 1. Watch how the offensive line, especially the interior, handles a better pass rush than it saw from Tennessee, and who is calling the shots in the front office.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars drop a London shootout, head to bye

stories.text: Jaguars lose 34-31 in London but still lead the AFC South
stories.summary: Cam Little's 60-yard field goal tied the game at 31 with 1:55 left, and Ka'imi Fairbairn won it for Houston as time expired. Jacksonville fell to 4-2 and ended a three-game winning streak. Trevor Lawrence threw for 306 yards and four touchdowns, but his end zone interception cost the Jaguars a scoring chance.

stories.text: Jaguars hope Montaric Brown and Ross Matiscik return after bye
stories.summary: Cornerback Montaric Brown (hamstring) and long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder) sat out the loss to Houston. The team hopes to get both back before its next game. Jacob Bobenmoyer, newly signed, handled long snapping in Matiscik's place.

stories.text: Travis Hunter scores and intercepts in the same game
stories.summary: Hunter caught four passes for 59 yards and a 7-yard touchdown, and he picked off Stroud in the end zone. He is the first NFL player since 2002 with a receiving touchdown and an interception in one game. Coach Liam Coen said the offense needs to keep getting him the ball, even though he played only nine offensive snaps.

stories.text: 15: snaps Brian Thomas Jr. played out of 70
stories.summary: Thomas played 15 of the Jaguars' 70 offensive snaps, a career low, and finished without a catch for the second straight game. Rookie Josh Cameron took 35 snaps in his place. Coen described the receiver's role as week to week, and Thomas enters the bye fourth in the rotation behind Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Cameron.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then the Colts on Nov. 1
stories.summary: Jacksonville is off this week. The Jaguars return on Nov. 1 against Indianapolis, a team they have beaten 11 straight times in Jacksonville. The extra week gives Coen time to settle the receiver rotation and get Brown and Matiscik healthy.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans finally win, rally past Colts 26-20

stories.text: Titans get Robert Saleh his first win with a 13-point rally
stories.summary: Tennessee trailed 13-0 at halftime in Indianapolis, then scored on all five second-half possessions to win 26-20. It was Saleh's first victory as head coach and the franchise's 500th all-time win. A blocked punt returned for a touchdown by Oluwafemi Oladejo gave the Titans their first lead.

stories.text: No Week 7 designations yet; Spears and Williams watched
stories.summary: The Titans have not released a Week 7 injury report. The last designations, from Week 6, had Kevin Winston Jr. and Jordan Elliott out, with Tyjae Spears and Joshua Williams questionable. Williams returned from a pectoral injury against the Colts and played well in a secondary where Alontae Taylor was a healthy scratch.

stories.text: Jeffery Simmons dominates in Indianapolis
stories.summary: Simmons had two sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery, and he passed Ted Washington for 10th on the franchise sack list with 46.5. He is the first defensive tackle since 2020 to post at least six tackles, two sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery in a game. He also drew seven pressures, per PFF.

stories.text: 213: yards the Titans were outgained and still won
stories.summary: Indianapolis beat Tennessee by 213 total yards, the worst yardage margin in a Titans win since 2006. The Titans survived on three takeaways, six sacks and a blocked-punt touchdown. Cam Ward threw for just 102 yards on 11 of 22 passing.

stories.text: Browns visit Nashville Sunday, Oct. 25, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Tennessee hosts Cleveland (4-2) at Nissan Stadium in Week 7. Saleh said the staff will ask the same hard questions after the first win, and that Ward is improving but has to play at a higher level. Watch Cleveland's pass rush against a Titans line that allowed no sacks last week.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Payton sticks with Nix as offense sputters

stories.text: Payton stands by Bo Nix after another ugly win
stories.summary: Denver beat Seattle in overtime on Thursday, but the offense gave Sean Payton little to like. Asked Monday whether he would change quarterbacks, Payton said no and pointed to the supporting cast as the thing that has to improve. Bo Nix is completing 60.3 percent of his passes, a career low, and averaging 5.6 yards per attempt, 32nd in the league.

stories.text: Surtain and Hufanga both missed the Seahawks game
stories.summary: Cornerback Patrick Surtain II sat out with an ankle injury, and safety Talanoa Hufanga went down with his own ankle injury against the Chargers on Oct. 11. ESPN reported Hufanga could miss two to three weeks, which might stretch to the Week 10 bye. Devon Key took his snaps at safety. Check Wednesday's practice report for where both stand before Arizona.

stories.text: McMillian picks off Darnold, Lutz wins it from 53
stories.summary: Cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian intercepted Sam Darnold on Seattle's opening overtime drive, at the Denver 43. Kicker Wil Lutz then hit a 53-yard field goal to end it, 17-14. J.K. Dobbins supplied the only offense of note, with 41 rushing yards and a 4-yard touchdown.

stories.text: 5: sacks by the Denver defense on Sam Darnold
stories.summary: The Broncos sacked Darnold five times and hit him 17 times in the overtime win. Nik Bonitto forced a fumble that Justin Strnad recovered at the Denver 34. Denver gained just 168 yards on offense, so the pass rush carried the night.

stories.text: Broncos visit Cardinals Sunday at 4:05 ET on CBS
stories.summary: Denver travels to State Farm Stadium in Glendale for a 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff on Sunday, Oct. 25, shown regionally on CBS. Watch whether Surtain and Hufanga return, and whether the offense finds any rhythm after back-to-back low passing totals for Nix.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs stay perfect, beat Chargers 22-6

stories.text: Chiefs beat Chargers 22-6 to stay unbeaten
stories.summary: Kansas City improved to 5-0, the only undefeated team left in the AFC, with a 22-6 win at Arrowhead. The defense forced two takeaways and sacked the quarterback four times. The Chiefs are 3-0 against the AFC West.

stories.text: Mahomes still hunting his burst after knee rehab
stories.summary: Patrick Mahomes has not missed a game this season, but he said he still lacks some burst in his left knee after last December's ACL and LCL tears. The Chiefs improved to 5-0 with the 22-6 win over the Chargers.

stories.text: Kenneth Walker runs for 128 and two scores
stories.summary: Running back Kenneth Walker III carried the offense with 128 yards and two touchdowns against the Chargers. His 665 rushing yards lead the NFL. Xavier Worthy added seven catches for 73 yards.

stories.text: 100: Mahomes wins in just 131 starts
stories.summary: Patrick Mahomes collected his 100th regular-season win in his 131st start, which ties Tom Brady for the fewest starts to reach 100. He threw no touchdown passes on the day, and the Chiefs still won by 16.

stories.text: Chiefs at Seahawks, Sunday Night Football 8:20 ET
stories.summary: Kansas City plays at Lumen Field in Seattle on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC, also streaming on Peacock. The Seahawks come in off a Thursday night overtime loss in Denver, their second defeat in five days.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Raiders drop third straight, 33-30 to Bills

stories.text: Raiders lose third in a row, 33-30 to the Bills
stories.summary: Las Vegas fell to 3-3 after an undefeated September. Kirk Cousins threw for 313 yards and two touchdowns, but one interception set up a Buffalo score and the Raiders went 2 for 5 in the red zone. Klint Kubiak's message for the week: close games out.

stories.text: Raiders keep an eye on Jeanty's ankle and foot
stories.summary: Rookie running back Ashton Jeanty has worked through an ankle injury since training camp and picked up a foot issue on top of it. Kubiak said he was progressing and could handle more practice work. Jeanty ran 10 times for 2.2 yards per carry against Buffalo. This report is thin on fresh designations, so confirm against Wednesday's official list.

stories.text: Tre Tucker posts 5 catches, 97 yards, 2 scores
stories.summary: Receiver Tre Tucker led the Raiders with 97 yards and two touchdowns, including a diving 44-yard score with 1:32 left. It was his third career game with multiple touchdown catches. The late touchdown made it a one-score game, but Buffalo held on.

stories.text: 165: yards from Bowers and Mayer combined
stories.summary: Tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer combined for 11 catches and 165 yards against the Bills. Mayer had a career-high 95 yards on seven catches, while Bowers finished with four for 70, and his first catch did not come until late in the third quarter.

stories.text: Rams visit Allegiant Stadium Sunday at 4:25 ET on Fox
stories.summary: Las Vegas hosts the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 4:25 p.m. ET on Fox. Both teams are coming off one-score losses, and the Raiders have been outscored by 26 points in third quarters this season, so watch the start of the second half.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Chargers 0-6, Harbaugh to review the offense

stories.text: Winless Chargers will look at everything on offense
stories.summary: Los Angeles fell to 0-6 with a 22-6 loss in Kansas City. The offense ranks last in the league in EPA per play and scores 15.0 points per game. Jim Harbaugh said he will examine every part of it during the bye week, and Justin Herbert called the output not good enough.

stories.text: Chargers carry a long list into the bye
stories.summary: Left tackle Joe Alt (neck), safety Derwin James Jr. (hamstring), receiver Tre' Harris (hamstring) and cornerback Donte Jackson (hamstring) all sat out the Chiefs game. Right tackle Rashawn Slater is on injured reserve, and center Tyler Biadasz is out for the year with a torn ACL. The bye gives the roster extra time to heal.

stories.text: Cam Hart picks off Mahomes in the end zone
stories.summary: Cornerback Cam Hart intercepted Patrick Mahomes in the end zone and later made another takeaway on third-and-goal from the 2. He has two interceptions this season. Quentin Johnston also had a 57-yard catch, the Chargers' longest play of the year.

stories.text: 15.0: points per game for the Chargers offense
stories.summary: Los Angeles averages 15.0 points per game and trails the league in EPA per play. On Sunday it reached the Chiefs' 1-yard line before a holding penalty and incompletions turned the drive into a field goal. Across four momentum swings, the offense ran 17 plays for 38 yards.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then the Rams on Nov. 1
stories.summary: The Chargers are off this weekend. They return Sunday, Nov. 1, at 1:05 p.m. PT (4:05 p.m. ET) against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium, shown on Fox. The Chargers are listed as the road team in the shared building.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys fall to 2-4 as offense stalls again

stories.text: Cowboys fall to 2-4 after 23-13 loss at Green Bay
stories.summary: Dallas dropped its second straight game on Sunday night at Lambeau Field. Brian Schottenheimer said he is very frustrated and blamed early deficits for pushing the offense into catch-up mode. The Cowboys have scored 29 points combined over the last two games.

stories.text: Winters out with Achilles strain, Overshown nears return
stories.summary: Linebacker Dee Winters strained his Achilles in the second quarter against the Packers and will likely miss time, according to Stephen Jones. DeMarvion Overshown, sidelined since a Week 1 hamstring injury, has a great chance to play Monday night, likely on the weak side. KaVontae Turpin left the game with damaged rib cartilage and has no timeline yet.

stories.text: Prescott throws 54 times, gets no help from the run
stories.summary: Dak Prescott went 34 of 54 for 258 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in Green Bay. He averaged 4.3 yards per attempt, the fourth lowest of his career since 2018 per Next Gen Stats. Prescott said the offense did not hold its own against a defense that played well.

stories.text: 48: rushing yards, a season low for Dallas
stories.summary: The Cowboys ran for just 48 yards against the Packers. After Javonte Williams scored with 9:19 left in the third quarter, they called only one more run. Prescott's 54 pass attempts tied for the fourth most of his career.

stories.text: At Eagles, Monday night at 8:15 ET on ESPN/ABC
stories.summary: Dallas visits Philadelphia at Lincoln Financial Field on Monday, Oct. 26, in the third NFC East game of its season. The Eagles are 2-4 and start Tanner McKee at quarterback while Jalen Hurts sits on injured reserve. Watch whether the Cowboys can run the ball enough to keep Prescott out of long yardage.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants QB call looms after McCarthy's rally

stories.text: Harbaugh holds off on naming Giants QB for Houston
stories.summary: J.J. McCarthy replaced Jameis Winston with the Giants down 34-10 early in the fourth quarter and pulled New York within a score before the final fourth-down throw fell incomplete. John Harbaugh would not name a Week 7 starter and said he has no problem with Winston. The Giants lost 34-27 to the Saints.

stories.text: Newsome leaves with concussion, Thomas cleared
stories.summary: Cornerback Newsome left the Saints game in the third quarter with a concussion and was ruled out. Left tackle Thomas went for a concussion evaluation in the fourth quarter and was cleared. Wide receiver Mooney appeared on the in-game report with a neck injury. Colton Hood, Tyler Nubin, Jermaine Eluemunor and Theo Johnson were all inactive.

stories.text: Nabers posts 12 catches for 165 yards in the loss
stories.summary: Malik Nabers caught 12 of 15 targets for 165 yards against the Saints. The 12 catches tied his career high and gave him a third straight 100-yard game, all while the quarterback spot shifted around him.

stories.text: 243: McCarthy's passing yards in 11 minutes
stories.summary: McCarthy threw for 243 yards in about 11 minutes of work and totaled 271 yards. His passing total tied Eli Manning's 2012 mark for the most by a Giants quarterback in at least 35 years. His 271 total yards rank second among fourth-quarter quarterbacks since 1991, behind Drew Brees.

stories.text: At Texans, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Giants visit Houston on Sunday, Oct. 25, and the Texans are 2-4 after winning their last game in London. Houston coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed receiver Tank Dell will play for the first time in over two years. Watch who starts under center for New York, which goes into its bye after this game.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles lose Hurts and a fourth straight

stories.text: Hurts likely done for 2026 after blood clots found
stories.summary: Doctors found blood clots in Jalen Hurts' lungs along with a deep vein thrombosis, and the Eagles placed him on injured reserve Oct. 17. The earliest he can return is Week 11 against the Steelers. The team and his agent expect a full recovery. Tanner McKee takes over the offense.

stories.text: Steele, Smith Jr. and Davis ruled out in Carolina loss
stories.summary: Running back Carson Steele (shoulder), linebacker Nolan Smith Jr. (concussion) and defensive tackle Jordan Davis (right leg) all left the Panthers game and did not return. Receiver Dontayvion Wicks went down with a right ankle injury. Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was among the inactives.

stories.text: DeVonta Smith bright spot with 7 catches, 75 yards, TD
stories.summary: DeVonta Smith led Philadelphia's receivers with seven catches for 75 yards and a touchdown in the 25-14 loss to Carolina. Tanner McKee threw for 215 yards on 26 of 45 in his first start outside a Week 18 game, and the Eagles ran for only 35 yards as a team.

stories.text: 650: yards the Eagles have been outgained this year
stories.summary: Philadelphia has been outgained by 650 yards through six weeks, last among the league's 32 teams. Over the four-game losing streak the gap is 723 yards. Under-center dropbacks have a 15.2% success rate, the worst mark in the NFL.

stories.text: Cowboys visit Monday at 8:15 ET on ESPN/ABC
stories.summary: Dallas comes to Lincoln Financial Field on Monday, Oct. 26. McKee is expected to start, and Nick Sirianni says Sean Mannion keeps calling plays. Watch whether the Eagles can move the ball on early downs after punting on their first five possessions against Carolina.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: McLaurin knee scare clouds Commanders' bye

stories.text: Commanders fall short in late rally against 49ers
stories.summary: Washington lost 23-17 on Monday night after trailing 23-3 late in the third quarter. The Commanders outgained San Francisco 224 to 72 in the second half and had two drives inside the 49ers' territory in the final two minutes, but the last snap ended in a sack.

stories.text: McLaurin carted off, Quinn fears a significant injury
stories.summary: Terry McLaurin went down on a route late in the first quarter with a left knee injury and left the field with an air cast. Dan Quinn said it could be significant and that there is fear testing on Tuesday will show a major problem. McLaurin has 15 catches for 230 yards and a touchdown in five games.

stories.text: Daniels throws for 300 yards in the comeback try
stories.summary: Jayden Daniels went 29 of 40 for 300 yards and two touchdowns against San Francisco, both scores coming in the second half. Nine Washington receivers caught a pass even after McLaurin left early.

stories.text: 224-72: Washington's second-half yardage edge
stories.summary: The Commanders managed 90 yards and two first downs in the first half and then outgained the 49ers 224 to 72 after the break. The 49ers led 20-3 at halftime and finished with four sacks.

stories.text: Bye in Week 7, then the Eagles in prime time Nov. 1
stories.summary: Washington rests this week and returns on Nov. 1 against the visiting Eagles in a prime-time game, listed on NBC's Sunday Night Football. Philadelphia is 2-4. Watch the McLaurin test results and how Quinn rebuilds the receiver group over the bye.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Williams back, Bears host Patriots on TNF

stories.text: Williams returns from hamstring tear and Bears beat Falcons 31-23
stories.summary: Caleb Williams missed three games, then came back and completed his first 12 passes in Atlanta. He finished 30 of 36 for 305 yards and a touchdown with no turnovers. Chicago led 31-7 before Atlanta made the final margin closer, and the win moved the Bears to 4-2.

stories.text: Edwards, Stevenson and Monangai sat out in Atlanta
stories.summary: Running back Kyle Monangai was inactive with turf toe, and linebacker T.J. Edwards and cornerback Tyrique Stevenson were among the defenders missing against the Falcons. Guard Jonah Jackson went into that game doubtful with a hip injury. Official Week 7 designations arrive with the first practice report this week.

stories.text: Kyler Gordon debuts with three sacks and a game-sealing strip
stories.summary: Gordon returned from a calf injury and sacked Michael Penix Jr. three times, two of them strip-sacks. The second forced a fumble that Devin Bush recovered at the Atlanta 28 with 2:54 left. That sealed the Bears' win.

stories.text: 712: Williams' passing yards in three appearances
stories.summary: Williams has 712 passing yards, three passing touchdowns and two rushing touchdowns in three appearances this season. The Bears scored 90 points in the two games he started and finished. Chicago is 2-1 when he starts.

stories.text: Patriots visit Soldier Field on Thursday night
stories.summary: Chicago hosts New England (4-2) on Thursday, Oct. 22 at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video, on a short week. Both teams carry top-10 defensive numbers, and the Patriots have won three straight. Williams and Drake Maye meet for the second time since their 2024 matchup.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions off bye, healing up for Packers

stories.text: Lions enter bye on a 45-21 win and chase second place
stories.summary: Detroit beat Arizona 45-21 before its Week 6 bye and sits at 3-2, tied for second in the NFC North with Chicago and Green Bay. Minnesota leads the division at 5-0. The Lions now host the Packers with a chance to reshuffle the standings.

stories.text: Lions lose Kennedy for the year, White faces surgery
stories.summary: Tom Kennedy tore his MCL and will have surgery, ending his season. Devin White broke his arm and will also have surgery, with no clear timeline. Safety Brian Branch and lineman Cade Mays were expected back for Green Bay, though one preview lists Mays on injured reserve, so check the Wednesday report.

stories.text: Gibbs leads a run game with 504 yards and 7 scores
stories.summary: Through Week 5, Jahmyr Gibbs had 504 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns. Jared Goff had 1,485 passing yards and 12 touchdowns without an interception. The two drive the league's top scoring offense.

stories.text: 32.8: Lions points per game, first in the NFL
stories.summary: Detroit scored 32.8 points per game through Week 5, tops in the league. The defense went the other way, allowing 29.6 points and 404.4 yards per game, the most yards in the league. Those numbers set up a shootout with Green Bay.

stories.text: Packers visit Ford Field on Sunday afternoon
stories.summary: Detroit hosts Green Bay (4-2) on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX at Ford Field. Watch whether Branch and Mays return to a defense that has leaked yards.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers win three straight, Jacobs cleared to play

stories.text: Josh Jacobs comes off the commissioner exempt list
stories.summary: The NFL removed Jacobs from the Commissioner Exempt List on Monday, so he is eligible for Week 7. Green Bay has not said whether he will play, and he has not appeared in a game this season. The league's investigation under the personal conduct policy continues.

stories.text: Cisse stinger, Lloyd and Kraft scares after Dallas win
stories.summary: Rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse left the Dallas game with a shoulder stinger. MarShawn Lloyd and Tucker Kraft each left briefly and returned. Defensive tackle Javon Hargrave and linebacker Edgerrin Cooper are out for the season with Achilles injuries.

stories.text: Golden posts 104 yards and a touchdown against Dallas
stories.summary: Matthew Golden caught six passes for 104 yards and the touchdown from Jordan Love. Love threw for 276 yards and one interception, taking three sacks. Green Bay won 23-13 at Lambeau Field.

stories.text: 57: rushing yards in a win, with Jacobs still away
stories.summary: Green Bay ran for 57 yards against Dallas, led by Pierre Strong Jr. with 28 on 11 carries. The Packers entered the game averaging 60 rushing yards a game, the lowest in the NFL. Jacobs has not played this season.

stories.text: Packers go to Detroit seeking a fourth straight win
stories.summary: Green Bay (4-2) visits Detroit (3-2) on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX at Ford Field. The Packers' offense converted a league-low 27.6 percent of third downs entering Week 6 before going 9 of 10 in the first half against Dallas. Watch whether that carries over.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Unbeaten Vikings return from bye to host Colts

stories.text: Vikings reach the bye 5-0 after beating the Saints
stories.summary: Minnesota won 23-13 in New Orleans on Oct. 11, its second 5-0 start in three seasons. The Vikings are one of three unbeaten teams left in the NFL. Kevin O'Connell said the bye came at a good time to heal.

stories.text: Hockenson, Addison, Mason and Darrisaw due back after bye
stories.summary: O'Connell expects tight end T.J. Hockenson (concussion) back for the Colts. Jordan Addison (hamstring), Jordan Mason (thumb) and tackle Christian Darrisaw (concussion) are also expected after the bye. Guard Donovan Jackson and tight end Josh Oliver are out for the season.

stories.text: Kyler Murray: 40 of 48 over his last six quarters
stories.summary: Murray completed his first 12 passes against the Saints and has thrown for 364 yards over his last six quarters with no turnovers. He also ran 10 times for 51 yards in that stretch. Justin Jefferson caught the go-ahead touchdown from Murray early in the third quarter.

stories.text: 34: straight field goals made by Will Reichard
stories.summary: Reichard made three more field goals against the Saints, stretching his streak to 34 straight makes. Andrew Van Ginkel's sack extended Minnesota's run of games with at least one sack to 33. Both streaks carry into Sunday.

stories.text: Colts come to U.S. Bank Stadium without Sauce Gardner
stories.summary: Minnesota hosts Indianapolis (2-4) on Sunday, Oct. 25 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf) is expected to miss the game, and Indianapolis lost to the Titans last Sunday. Former Viking Daniel Jones is the Colts' quarterback.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons stuck at 0-3 at home after Bears loss

stories.text: Falcons fall to 0-3 at home as Bears build a 31-7 lead
stories.summary: Chicago won 31-23 at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, and Atlanta has now lost two straight. The Falcons trailed 14-0 early and 31-7 late before a fourth-quarter rally came up short. Rookie Zachariah Branch lost two fumbles on returns, and the team released Cooper Rush and signed Andy Dalton.

stories.text: Rookie LB Kendal Daniels is out of the hospital after neck scare
stories.summary: Daniels left the field on a stretcher after a tackle against Chicago, and coach Kevin Stefanski called Monday's news on him all positive. He is back at the team facility. Stefanski had no update on whether Daniels can play against San Francisco, so his status stays open until practice reports arrive.

stories.text: Kyle Pitts scores twice in the fourth quarter to keep Atlanta alive
stories.summary: Pitts caught five of seven targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns against Chicago. Both scores came in the fourth quarter as Atlanta cut a 24-point hole to eight. Jahan Dotson added a team-high 87 receiving yards and a touchdown on three catches.

stories.text: 56.4%: Chicago pressured Michael Penix Jr. on more than half his dropbacks
stories.summary: Next Gen Stats tracked pressure on 56.4 percent of Penix's dropbacks, the highest rate the Bears have posted in a game this season. He went down five times, three by Kyler Gordon. Against 22 blitzes, Penix still completed 10 of 18 passes for 121 yards and three touchdowns.

stories.text: Falcons host the 49ers Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Atlanta plays San Francisco at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 25, with kickoff at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. The Falcons are still chasing their first home win of the season. Watch whether the offense starts faster and whether the line holds up better against pressure.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers win in Philly despite 13 penalties

stories.text: Bryce Young and Panthers beat the Eagles 25-14 on the road
stories.summary: Carolina improved to 3-2 and handed Philadelphia its fourth straight loss. Young threw for 281 yards and two touchdowns, both to Tommy Tremble. Running back Chuba Hubbard called Young a one-of-one player after the game.

stories.text: Phillips and Incoom hurt on defense against Philadelphia
stories.summary: Outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips aggravated a hamstring injury, and outside linebacker Thomas Incoom suffered a calf injury. Neither has an official status for Sunday yet. Carolina already ran a thin secondary in Philadelphia.

stories.text: Chuba Hubbard runs for 120 yards and a score in Philadelphia
stories.summary: Hubbard carried 28 times for 120 yards and a one-yard touchdown. He has now topped 100 rushing yards in back to back games. He also converted a fourth-and-1 with a 19-yard run during Carolina's long second-half push.

stories.text: 149: penalty yards Carolina gave up on 13 flags and still won
stories.summary: The Panthers drew 13 penalties for 149 yards at Philadelphia. They still outgained the Eagles 399 to 222 and did not turn the ball over. Many of the early flags stalled drives in Eagles territory and held the offense to 10 first-half points.

stories.text: Panthers host Tampa Bay Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Carolina plays the Buccaneers at Bank of America Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1 p.m. ET on Fox. It is Tampa Bay's first division game of the year, and the Bucs have won 12 of the last 15 meetings. Watch whether Tampa Bay gets quarterback Baker Mayfield back from his thumb injury.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints end skid, then head to Paris

stories.text: Saints beat the Giants 34-27 to snap a three-game losing streak
stories.summary: New Orleans moved to 2-4 after scoring on five straight drives to erase an early 10-0 deficit. The Saints led 34-10 after three quarters and held off a late Giants rally. They now travel to Paris to face Pittsburgh.

stories.text: Tyson and Elliss make the Paris trip; Ruiz status unclear
stories.summary: Coach Kellen Moore said receiver Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) and linebacker Kaden Elliss (calf) both traveled with the team. Either could play against the Steelers, though neither is cleared. Guard Cesar Ruiz left the Giants game late in the second quarter and has no update yet.

stories.text: Martin Emerson Jr. picks off two passes against the Giants
stories.summary: Emerson had two interceptions, four passes defended and seven solo tackles, matching career highs in interceptions and pass breakups. Julian Blackmon added a fourth-quarter pick. The defense finished with four takeaways and five sacks, both season highs for the unit.

stories.text: 175: rushing yards, a season high, drive the Saints past New York
stories.summary: New Orleans ran for 175 yards against the Giants and held the ball for 31:02. Tyler Shough added 32 yards on five carries, including a one-yard touchdown. The Saints also went three for three in the red zone.

stories.text: Saints face Steelers in Paris Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network
stories.summary: New Orleans plays Pittsburgh at Stade de France in Paris on Sunday, Oct. 25. Kickoff is 9:30 a.m. ET (8:30 a.m. CT) on NFL Network. Watch how the Saints handle the travel and early start, and whether Tyson returns.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs blow 16-3 lead, fall to 1-5 in overtime

stories.text: Bucs lose 26-19 in overtime after leading Pittsburgh 16-3
stories.summary: Tampa Bay fell to 1-5 at home. Pittsburgh scored on consecutive fourth-quarter possessions, Chase McLaughlin's 53-yard field goal forced overtime, and Aaron Rodgers then drove 70 yards for the winning touchdown. Coach Todd Bowles said the team has no margin for error.

stories.text: Baker Mayfield's thumb gets its test on Wednesday
stories.summary: Mayfield has a dislocated right thumb and has missed three straight starts. Bowles said Monday that Wednesday's practice will show whether Mayfield can play at Carolina. Tampa Bay is preparing as if rookie Jalon Daniels starts again.

stories.text: David Walker leads the pass rush with two sacks
stories.summary: Walker finished with two sacks, five tackles and three quarterback hits against Pittsburgh. He is the first Buc with multiple sacks in a game since Anthony Nelson last October. The defense posted five sacks and seven tackles for loss, both season highs.

stories.text: 48: Josiah Trotter's tackles, most by a Buc through five games since 2000
stories.summary: Trotter made 11 tackles and broke up a pass against the Steelers. His 48 tackles are the most by a Tampa Bay player through five games since at least 2000. Zyon McCollum also set a career high with 11 tackles.

stories.text: Bucs visit the Panthers Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Tampa Bay plays at Carolina on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1 p.m. ET on Fox at Bank of America Stadium. It is the Bucs' first division game of the season. Watch the quarterback decision and whether the defense can keep up its pass rush.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Six Ryland kicks stun the Rams

stories.text: Cardinals beat Rams 18-16 on Ryland's last-second kick
stories.summary: Arizona went to SoFi Stadium and won without scoring a touchdown. Chad Ryland hit a 43-yard field goal as time expired after a 15-yard penalty on the Rams moved the Cardinals into range. The win lifts Arizona to 2-4 and puts it ahead of Los Angeles in the NFC West through the head-to-head result.

stories.text: Jeremiyah Love expected to run Tuesday after ankle absence
stories.summary: The rookie running back sat out the Rams game with an ankle problem that lingered for weeks. Coach Mike LaFleur said Monday that Love should do some running Tuesday. Whether he can play Sunday against Denver is still open, and Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will keep the carries until he is cleared.

stories.text: Chad Ryland goes 6 for 6 and wins it at the gun
stories.summary: Ryland supplied every Arizona point in Week 6 with six made field goals, the last one from 43 yards as the clock hit zero. Special teams also won the field position fight, with the Cardinals netting 40 yards per punt to the Rams' 27.7. A kicker who accounts for the whole scoreboard is the reason this team has a second win.

stories.text: 0: Touchdowns on five red zone trips, and Arizona still won
stories.summary: The Cardinals reached the red zone five times against the Rams and settled for field goals every time. Four drives ran 10 plays or longer, all after the first quarter, and Arizona held the ball for 34:52 to the Rams' 25:08. The offense moved the ball. It needs to finish drives with touchdowns.

stories.text: Cardinals host Broncos Sunday at 4:05 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Arizona plays Denver at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Sunday, October 25, with CBS carrying the game. The Cardinals are chasing their first win streak of the season. Watch whether Love returns and whether the defense that pressured Matthew Stafford can repeat the effort.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams lose Adams and fall to 2-4

stories.text: Rams drop to 2-4 with 18-16 home loss to Arizona
stories.summary: Los Angeles managed fewer than 100 yards at the half and had three three-and-outs before a late rally fell short. Matthew Stafford hit Colby Parkinson for a touchdown with 47 seconds left, but Arizona drove for the winning field goal. The preseason Super Bowl favorite is now 2-4.

stories.text: Adams out 6 to 10 weeks, Turner to IR, Ford and Grupe done
stories.summary: Coach Sean McVay said Davante Adams has a hamstring injury and will miss six to 10 weeks. Defensive lineman Kobie Turner heads to injured reserve with a groin injury for four to six weeks. Nose tackle Poona Ford (triceps) and kicker Blake Grupe are out for the season.

stories.text: Puka Nacua keeps producing as the passing game narrows
stories.summary: Nacua caught six passes for 80 yards against Arizona and now carries more of the receiving load with Adams down. Stafford finished 25 of 33 for 222 yards and two touchdowns, below the 300-yard pace he held in the previous four games. The Rams will lean on Nacua until the receiver room gets help.

stories.text: 25:08: Rams' time of possession in the loss to Arizona
stories.summary: Arizona held the ball for 34:52 while Los Angeles had it for 25:08. The Rams also had fewer than 100 yards at halftime. Punter Ethan Evans filled in at kicker after Grupe left with a knee injury on the opening kickoff.

stories.text: Rams visit Raiders Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Los Angeles plays at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on Sunday, October 25, with Fox broadcasting. The Rams need a kicker, a receiver to pair with Nacua and a healthy defensive line. The Raiders are 3-3 and Kirk Cousins threw for 313 yards in their Week 6 loss to Buffalo.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers go 6-0, survive a late scare

stories.text: 49ers hold off Commanders 23-17 to start 6-0
stories.summary: San Francisco led 20-3 at halftime and then watched Washington cut it to one score in the fourth quarter. The defense closed it out with four sacks, including an 18-yard sack on the final play. The win gave the 49ers their 56th Monday Night Football victory, the most in NFL history.

stories.text: Mike Evans' Achilles flares up, Shanahan hopeful for Sunday
stories.summary: Evans left Monday's game before halftime when his Achilles tendonitis acted up. Kyle Shanahan said he does not view it as a long-term issue and hopes Evans can play Sunday in Atlanta. Safety Marques Sigle (ankle) also got hurt, and Nick Bosa is still working back from a calf injury.

stories.text: Christian McCaffrey scores twice and touches it 25 times
stories.summary: McCaffrey ran for two 1-yard touchdowns and caught nine passes for 53 yards, 117 yards from scrimmage in all. He has rushed for a touchdown in five straight games and has seven rushing scores this season. It was his 71st career game with 100 or more scrimmage yards.

stories.text: 105.6: Purdy's career passer rating, best in NFL history
stories.summary: Brock Purdy went 21 of 29 for 264 yards and a touchdown against Washington. His career passer rating now stands at 105.6, the highest of any quarterback with at least 1,500 attempts, ahead of Lamar Jackson's 102.7. His 30 touchdown passes to George Kittle tie the franchise record for a quarterback and tight end pair.

stories.text: 49ers visit Falcons Sunday at 1 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: San Francisco plays at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta on Sunday, October 25, on a short week after Monday night. The 49ers won last year's meeting 20-10. Watch the status of Evans and Bosa and whether the pass rush keeps getting to the quarterback.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Seahawks fall in OT, face Chiefs next

stories.text: Seahawks lose 17-14 in overtime at Denver to fall to 3-3
stories.summary: Seattle outgained Denver 353 yards to 168 and still lost on Wil Lutz's 53-yard field goal in overtime. The loss ended the Seahawks' seven-game prime-time winning streak, the longest in the NFL. Seattle scored 11 points in the final six minutes of regulation to force overtime but could not finish.

stories.text: Smith-Njigba played through an ankle injury at Denver
stories.summary: Jaxon Smith-Njigba dealt with an ankle problem during the week of practice and still played the full game in Denver. The report mentions no other Seattle injuries from the loss. The team will have extra days to heal before Sunday night.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba catches 12 for 134 after a quiet half
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba had two catches for 11 yards in the first half and then took over. He finished with 12 receptions on 16 targets for 134 yards, the best offensive performance on the field. Seattle will keep feeding him against a Kansas City defense.

stories.text: 51: Darnold's career-high pass attempts in the loss
stories.summary: Sam Darnold threw a career-high 51 times for 278 yards, with two interceptions and a 52.6 passer rating. Seattle has 12 turnovers in six games, seven of them Darnold interceptions. He has three multi-interception games already, the same number he had all of last season.

stories.text: Seahawks host Chiefs on Sunday Night Football, 8:20 PM ET
stories.summary: Seattle hosts Kansas City at Lumen Field on Sunday, October 25, on NBC and Peacock. The Chiefs are 5-0 and former Seahawks back Kenneth Walker III leads the NFL with 665 rushing yards. Seattle has not allowed a 100-yard rusher in 35 games, the league's longest streak.
